reviews.decision_reason: map_coverage preserves the eight allowed handoff need records and maps exact need text to supplied capabilities, producing direct coverage only when a matching capability_id exists. The observed final coverage matches this behavior, so no behaviorally significant fault is localized here.

prioritize_needs inverts unsupported status by setting unsupported = coverage == 'direct'. This causes covered needs to be ranked before truly unsupported needs and marks direct coverage rows as unsupported. The final priorities therefore select record n06-r02 as the top priority while actual unsupported records n06-r01 and n06-r07 are pushed to priorities 7 and 8. This is the top root-cause boundary for the wrong deterministic recommendation.

synthesize_recommendation retains the explicit eight-row priority window and derives the recommendation from the first already-ranked priority. Its output is deterministic given the incoming priorities; the bad top_need is inherited from the upstream priority ordering, not introduced here.

select_demand_records selects all supplied records with demand_score >= 3, which includes the full eight-record corpus. The fallback path does not introduce unrelated records or generic keyword matches in the supplied package.

normalize_evidence preserves the bounded allowed-record window, normalizes numeric demand and source fields, and emits the same eight demand records for downstream handoff. No missing or contradictory evidence in the supplied package localizes a fault here.

assemble_provenance ranks the normalized needs by descending demand_score with record_id tie-break. The resulting evidence_sources handoff has matching producer and consumer hashes, so downstream received the upstream provenance exactly.
